name: MultiMaster
blurb: The oscillating tool that invented the category, and still the one that sets the standard. Fein’s MultiMaster turns one compact body into a saw, scraper, sander, and detail cutter for the jobs a circular saw can’t reach. The German build is dense, and vibration stays controlled so the work can go longer without fatigue. If the kit has only one specialty power tool, this is the one.

name: CXS 18 Compact Drill
blurb: A compact cordless drill, short and balanced, made for hangings, furniture, and light assembly rather than the bulk of a full-size driver. Festool’s clutch and electronics make clean holes and careful seating the default, not a struggle.

name: E20C Claw Hammer
blurb: One-piece forged steel, a leather grip, and a balance that settles on the first swing. Estwing’s E20C is the classic American claw hammer, built for picture hanging, trim, and light framing.

name: DFH12 Rubber Mallet
blurb: A rubber mallet for force without scars. Soft face for seating joints, stuck parts, and assembly where a steel hammer would mark the surface. It sits next to the claw hammer.

name: SwissGrip Screwdriver Set
blurb: Swiss-made drivers with that unmistakable PB feel: precise tips, confident torsion, and grips that stay planted. A proper SwissGrip set covers the fasteners a house actually has, without the stripped screws of a cheap kit.

name: ESD Micro Bit Set
blurb: Electronics, eyeglasses, small appliances, and modern gadgets all ask for bits that full-size drivers can’t touch. Wiha’s ESD micro set is organized, precise, and built to a standard hobby kits don’t reach.

name: Type 81S Torpedo Level
blurb: A pocket torpedo that reads true and survives real use. Stabila’s vials are legendary for a reason: clear, stable, and trustworthy for hangings, shelves, and appliance leveling. The compact die-cast body lives in a drawer or a bag.

name: Self-Centering 25' Tape
blurb: A 25-foot tape with self-centering scales that cut the mental math when locating midpoints. Lufkin’s blade and case are sturdy, the printing is clean, and the hook behaves.

name: ST-350 Toolbox
blurb: The Trusco ST-350 is a compact steel toolbox, rigid and well finished, small enough to leave out rather than hide in a garage. It holds a small kit without becoming a junk drawer.

name: Pliers Set
blurb: German pliers, built so the jaws meet cleanly and the handles hold under a firm grip. A tight Knipex set covers gripping, cutting, and adjustment for plumbing fixtures, fasteners, wire, and the odd stuck nut.

name: DISTO D2
blurb: A pocket laser for length, width, and the diagonal that is otherwise a guess. Leica’s optics and Bluetooth keep the reading stable enough to work from, for hangings, furniture, and floor plans. It sits next to the tape.

name: ACTIK CORE
blurb: A rechargeable headlamp that leaves both hands free for wiring, attics, and evening work. Petzl’s beam is even, the CORE battery recharges instead of eating disposables, and the strap stays put.

name: Contour Profile Gauge
blurb: A profile gauge copies a shape that is hard to measure: baseboard, tile, a pipe in a wall, so the next piece can be marked cleanly. Shinwa’s stainless pins are finer than the plastic versions, so the curve stays accurate.

name: HyFlex 11-800
blurb: A light-assembly glove with a 15-gauge nylon liner and a foam nitrile palm, for handling and grip on dry or slightly oily work. Breathable enough to keep on, with the dexterity a house actually needs, and no latex.

name: EHK Trigger Clamp
blurb: A one-handed trigger clamp, the third hand for glue-ups, holding work, and assembly. It clamps or spreads, and the pads keep the bar from marking the piece.

name: S-type 26B Craft Knife
blurb: A pencil-length craft knife with a 1mm single-bevel blade, slide-adjustable, for paper, veneer, scoring, and light whittling. The blade is reversible, and a brass screw locks it.

name: Herring Blade
blurb: A flat utility knife with a magnetic latch and no moving parts. It takes standard 18mm snap blades and sits thin enough for a pocket.

name: 500-196-32 Digimatic Caliper
blurb: A 6-inch digital caliper for outside, inside, depth, and step. It wakes on the true reading after power-off, so there is no re-zeroing, at a resolution a tape cannot do.

name: 650 Scratch Awl
blurb: A scratch awl for scribing metal, starting screw holes, and piercing. The 3.5-inch chrome-plated shank is heat-treated, and the Cushion-Grip handle stays planted.

name: 300 Lead Holder
blurb: A 2.0 mm lead holder for marking lumber, tile, metal, and other surfaces a 0.5 mm lead will not survive. The hex barrel has a clutch, a lead-grade dial, and a sharpener under the cap.

name: Flip-N-Lite 5'
blurb: A 5-foot aluminum stepladder for bulbs, high shelves, and paint. It opens with one hand and folds to four inches, with extra-wide steps, a large standing platform, a tall handrail, and a tool tray on top. A chair is the wrong tool for this work.

name: 9.5" Ryoba
blurb: A 9.5-inch Japanese pull saw with rip teeth on one edge and cross-cut on the other. For trim, lumber, and a clean cut where a circular saw is too much. Rattan-wrapped handle, thin blade.

name: 3410 Right-Angle Light
blurb: A right-angle flashlight for the attic, the panel, and under the sink. The head articulates, spot and flood can run together or alone, and a magnetic clip holds it so both hands stay free. The body glows in the dark.

name: F-2
blurb: A bypass pruner for live wood. Forged aluminum handles, hardened steel blade, wire-cutting notch, and every part replaceable.

name: BugView HU-10
blurb: A one-hand bug catcher with a 5x acrylic lens. Catch, view, release, without crushing the specimen.

name: MF50 Air Duster
blurb: A cordless air duster for keyboards, vents, and the car, the work a can of air used to do. Three speeds, USB-C, four nozzles.

name: NCVT2P
blurb: A dual-range non-contact voltage tester, 12–1000V or 70–1000V AC. Visual and audible, CAT IV 1000V, pocket clip. For outlets, breakers, and doorbells.

name: Satsuki 7"
blurb: Sanjo-forged Satsuki scissors for thin branches up to about 1/8 inch. Long slim handles for canopy work, and for garden or ikebana.

name: SCS-2 7" Scissors
blurb: Seven-inch stainless scissors with one serrated edge. For fabric, plastic, rubber, and kitchen work. Ambidextrous ABS handles.

name: 217 Hedge Shears
blurb: Short white-oak handles and 175mm Izumo Yasugi blades. For topiary and other tight cuts.

name: 13 72 8 Wire Stripper
blurb: An 8-inch forged stripper for 10–20 AWG solid or stranded. Locating ridges on the jaws, and it cuts 6-32 and 8-32 screws without threading. Works on NM-B, BX, and MC.

name: BGA 50
blurb: A cordless AK blower for the driveway and patio, where noise matters. About 455 CFM and 123 mph. Kit with AK 20 battery and AL 101 charger.

name: 212Z-LH-12 Imperial
blurb: An imperial Rainbow hex L-key set with ball ends and a clip. Inch sizes only. Separate from the metric set.

name: 625 Ergo Scraper
blurb: A carbide-edge hand scraper for paint and surface prep. Triangle blade, belt holster.

name: 212LH-10 Metric
blurb: A metric chrome ball-end hex L-key set in the red clip. Millimeter sizes only. Separate from the imperial Rainbow set.

name: Putty Knives
blurb: Seki stainless putty knives in three widths: rounded 15/16", 3", and 4". Full tang, checkered handles.

name: Micro Whistle
blurb: A pealess Micro whistle that works wet. Loud, no cork to freeze or stick.
